source.title: Mean-field analysis for heavy ball methods: Dropout-stability, connectivity, and global convergence
source.authors: Di-Yuan Wu; V. Kungurtsev; Marco Mondelli

record.tranche_reason: The paper proves a global-convergence result for a three-layer mean-field heavy-ball training dynamics, using a population-risk objective rather than benchmark training classification error.
record.gate_note: The paper does not test any listed version's benchmark error, depth, initialization, learning-rate, or normalization claims. Its dropout-stability experiments measure a different outcome and are not rows for these versions.
record.test_reason: The study establishes conditional population-risk optimality for three-layer mean-field heavy-ball dynamics and studies dropout stability and connectivity. These outcomes do not test V1–V6. Mentioning spurious minima and initialization schemes does not test the specified width or initialization effects.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the global-optimality result is conditional on the specified mode of convergence and concerns the three-layer mean-field dynamics. Finite-width approximation bounds do not establish finite-network convergence to a global optimum.
record.recipe_differences: The paper analyzes stochastic heavy-ball training through a mean-field limit and proves a conditional population-risk convergence theorem; the listed versions concern other methods, settings, and outcomes.
record.method_sensitivity: The global-convergence result requires a three-layer network, a universal-approximation activation, full-support first-layer initialization, convex loss in the output, and an assumed mode of convergence.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 7.2 establishes optimal limiting population risk for three-layer mean-field heavy-ball dynamics under Assumptions 3.3 and 7.1 and output-convex loss; convergence in the specified mode is assumed.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the stated regularity, approximation, initialization, and convergence assumptions, three-layer mean-field heavy-ball dynamics attains the infimum population risk over prediction functions.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 6 bounds dropout error and loss along connecting paths; Section 8 reports dropout error decreasing as an inverse polynomial of width for two- and three-layer fully connected MNIST networks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Wide networks trained with stochastic heavy-ball dynamics exhibit dropout stability and low-loss connectivity in the studied mean-field setting.

record.problems: The global-convergence conclusion is conditional on an assumed mode of convergence, which the authors call technical; it concerns the mean-field limit, not finite-width benchmark classification. Numerical experiments address dropout error rather than the listed versions.
record.rows_left_out: No results omitted. The Section 8 dropout-error experiments do not measure outcomes named by the listed versions.

untested.parts: Finite convolutional networks reaching near-zero CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 training classification error, including random labels and size, stopping, or regularization effects.
Spurious-local-minimum frequency in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and the effect of adding one or two student neurons.
Training-error degradation with depth, identity-shortcut comparisons, and the stated special-initialization and normalization exceptions.
Initialization effects on training speed, signal and gradient propagation, and trainable depth; orthogonal versus Gaussian comparisons.
Loss, curvature, sharpness, recovery, and divergence around learning-rate stability thresholds.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, including Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: Dropout stability measures the population-loss change after removing neurons, rather than training error or avoidance of spurious local minima. Full-support initialization is an assumption, not a tested initialization advantage. The excluded dropout experiments are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 classification error, corrupted or random labels, finite convolutional networks, and the listed size, stopping, and regularization conditions.
Teacher-student ReLU local minima and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual network training error as depth changes, and the stated special-initialization or no-normalization conditions.
Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation, orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization, and very deep plain networks.
Training behavior around stability-limit learning rates, curvature or sharpness, and divergence.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

rows.subject: three-layer mean-field ODE
rows.size_stated: mean-field limit; finite widths not specified for this result
rows.operation_detail: Theorem 7.2 proves convergence of the mean-field ODE's population risk to the infimum over measurable prediction functions, under the stated assumptions.

conditions.value: Assumptions 3.3 and 7.1; loss convex in the network output
the mean-field ODE converges in the specified mode

rows.baseline: infimum population risk over functions ŷ: R^D → R
rows.value: lim_{t→∞} E_z R(y, f(x; W(t))) = inf_{ŷ: R^D → R} E_z R(y, ŷ(x))
rows.note: A theoretical population-risk result for the mean-field dynamics; it does not report classification error or a benchmark result.
rows.check: The theorem is accurately recorded as conditional population-risk optimality, but its observed state cannot describe any listed version. It establishes neither near-zero training classification error nor a comparison of local-minimum frequency, depth, initialization, stability thresholds, or normalization.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
